name: Attai
overview: Attai was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as a son of Rehoboam and Maacah. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Attai means 'timely' or possibly serves as an abbreviation of Athaiah. It is a proper name recorded in 2 Chronicles 11:20 and was not given by God, reflecting a common Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Attai as the son of Rehoboam and Maacah. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Attai's significance lies in his place within the royal lineage of Judah as a son of Rehoboam, the king who succeeded Solomon. His mention helps establish the genealogical and dynastic context of Judah's monarchy, underscoring the continuity of David's line through Rehoboam's descendants.
